issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify addGuestStudents(int): void, and the solution implements addGuestStudents(int). However, the template defines addGuestStudents with a different parameter list (int, boolean). This parameter mismatch will confuse students and prevent them from implementing or testing the expected method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the specification and solution: replace public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement */ }. If input validation is desired, add an overloaded helper method or perform validation inside the single-parameter method so the public API matches the exercise description and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int) but the template declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput). The solution implements addGuestStudents(int). This mismatch in the method signature (extra boolean parameter in the template) creates a mapping conflict: students following the textual specification or tests will expect a single-parameter method, while the starter code provides a different signature, causing confusion and possible compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } (remove the extra boolean parameter), or update the problem/tests to expect the two-parameter signature consistently.
